question: Will the Trump administration or a GOP state governor deploy armed officers or troops to a polling or early voting site in 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: US general elections from 2018 to 2024. None had armed federal, or GOP-governor-ordered, personnel deliberately posted at an open polling site; 18 U.S.C. 592 and many state laws ban it. That gives a base rate of a few percent. Two things push it up for 2026: Trump's 'I don't rule anything out or in' on ICE at the polls (Time, Oct 1), and Homan's 'go where we gotta go' after a GOP candidate asked for ICE at the polls. There is also a reported ICE swarm at a San Antonio polling site in the May primary, and early voting is starting under heavy ICE activity in Texas and elsewhere. Against that: Gen. Caine publicly denied any plan to send troops to polling sites (Aug 31); DHS said in February that ICE would not be at polling places; the DC Guard incident at a ballot dropbox was officially called a mistake, and dropboxes don't count anyway; lawsuits are pending; and the criteria require armed personnel within 250 ft, a deliberate deployment, and uncontroversial credible reporting. Incidental presence is excluded. The main route to YES is an ICE enforcement action at or next to a Texas or other early-voting site that gets credible coverage. Markets: no matching market found. The nearest Manifold market (Guard at polls, about 40% on Sep 1) is broader (unarmed help counts, any governor), so it is not an anchor. Live web search failed this run, so the evidence is thinner and I stayed close to the base rate plus the escalation signals.
